entry.confirm_signal: Basic setup: constant monotone tone while the throttle is at maximum. Advanced setup: after about 20 tones of that constant tone, a confirmation tone (the manual shows one note symbol, count not certain).
steps: Throttle signal at maximum before power is applied
Apply supply power; a constant monotone tone means programming mode is active
Advanced setup only: keep the throttle at maximum until about 20 tones have sounded; this works only after the basic setup has been completed once
Throttle to minimum; the menu items are sounded as 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 tones in turn

announce.description: Items are sounded as 1 to 5 equal tones. After an item is selected and the throttle returns to minimum, its values are sounded as 1, 2, 3 ... equal tones. Each sequence restarts when nothing is selected. Tone length and gaps are not stated.

select.description: Throttle to maximum while the wanted item or value is being sounded; the ESC answers with one tone. Selecting an item opens its values; selecting a value stores it.

skip.description: No skip. Leaving the throttle at minimum passes every item or value; the menu then restarts.

scheme.confirm_signal: One tone after each selection (item or value), per the manual's acknowledgement symbol; the manual draws one note per acknowledgement
scheme.exit: After a value is stored, throttle back to minimum arms the ESC when the arming signal sounds. Power can also be removed and re-applied to change a further item.
scheme.description: Power on with the throttle at maximum starts programming. The basic setup (constant tone, then stick positions) must have been done once. In the advanced setup, 20 tones after power-on enter the item menu. Throttle to minimum sounds items 1-5; throttle to maximum selects one. The values of that item are then sounded the same way; maximum throttle selects a value and stores it. One item is changed per power cycle.

values.name: brake active (when the stored neutral position leaves room for it)
on (learns the operating speed at the next start)

unknowns: Duration of one tone, gap between tones in a count and pause between two mode counts: not stated
Duration of the 20 interval tones before entry: not stated, so the time from power-on to the 2 confirmation tones is unmeasured
Whether maximum throttle selects during the count or only after the last tone of a count: not stated
Number of times the mode sequence repeats before it ends or restarts: not stated
Minimum supply voltage at which the menu is entered: not stated; ESC cell detection needs a voltage matching the cell count and a 1-20 V bench supply covers at most 4 cells at 4.2 V
Behaviour on a current-limited 3 A bench supply: not stated; the manuals say the ESC is to be powered from batteries only, power supplies are not allowed
Idle current of the ESC with the motor connected: not stated, needed to separate tones from the idle level when counting beeps from supply current

Whether the RC-Setup in YGE_rc_setup.pdf (unofficial English translation dated 2012, source ESC generation not named) applies unchanged to every model listed: the model manuals point to an RC-Setup / Knüppel-Setup manual without reproducing it
Whether Navy models and the 155 Navy Opto (forward/reverse; no governor in their data lists) have extra or fewer items than the 5 listed, or lack Speed control: not stated
Default value of each item: not stated in the RC-Setup text
Which tone count the ESC announces first within a value list: the Tip says the sequence starts with the previously set value; not tested
Count and tone of the acknowledgement after a selection: the manual's symbols are ambiguous in the text extraction (one note shown)
Voltage needed to enter setup on 155 models (2-8 cells) and on 8S/12S: not stated
BEC type of 8S/12S (linear or switching): not stated
Complete RC-Setup (stick) menu: the manual refers to a separate RC-Setup manual on www.yge.de that is not in the corpus; items, values, beep encoding, select and exit are unknown.
Beep durations, gaps and entry timings: not stated.
Whether the 20-interval-beep entry of the YGE mode setup (see yge-hv) applies to this ESC: not stated in this manual.
notes: The motor must be connected: the motor windings produce all tones. Without a motor no tones are heard.
Manuals state that the ESC may only be powered from batteries; power supplies are not allowed. The bench supply is outside the manual's intended use.
Power applied with the throttle at maximum enters programming; the manuals tell the user to unplug the battery, set the throttle to minimum and reconnect to leave without changes.

YGE_rc_setup.pdf is an unofficial translation (R. Whitehead, 2012) of YGE's RC-Setup; it is the only source of the menu. The model manuals in this file only say that stick programming exists and refer to it.

Basic setup (done before the advanced setup): throttle at maximum, power on, constant tone; then move the stick to the neutral position (fully back for no brake, in the bottom quarter for brake) and wait for the acknowledgement; this stores both end positions. Next the soft start is chosen with the stick position: maximum throttle for fastest, further back for softer, middle as a compromise; wait for the acknowledgement, then move the stick back and the ESC arms.
Stick positions of the basic setup are stored; throttle range is therefore learned in this procedure.

Tone sequences in normal operation: descending tones = receiver signal recognised; ascending tones = stop position recognised and ESC armed; after the descending tones, tones for cell count follow (n identical tones = n LiPo cells, 2-6 cells; above 6 cells a different high-low sequence).
NiMH is announced as 2 different high / low tones; free voltage as 2x2 low / high tones (default 12 V for the future PC setup).
Start-up sequences: 3 descending tones, cell tones, 3 ascending tones on 7S, 8S/12S, 40/60/100/120 V4, Navy V4 and 155; the 155 models give 2 high and 2 low tones for 7 and 8 cells.

YGE_YGE-7S.pdf: to enter RC-Setup the ESC must see full throttle at power-up; where a receiver outputs a stop signal at power-up this only works if the ESC is disconnected from the receiver, full throttle is given after binding and the ESC is plugged in again. A bench throttle source that outputs full throttle at power-on avoids this.

YGE_8S-12S_en.pdf and YGE_Bedienungsanleitung-8S-12S.pdf disagree on the brake steps (5 in the English edition, 3 in the German one) and on battery types (German edition adds 4-10 NiMH cells; English edition lists 2-3 LiPo only).
YGE_YGE-100-V4.pdf is titled for the L series 40 to 160 A but its type table lists 40, 60, 100 and 120 A.
On the 155 models the battery must be connected in a fixed order (negative first, then the thin positive lead for anti-spark, then the thick positive lead) before any throttle is given.

A fault stored in the ESC is cleared by powering up at full throttle and unplugging after the interval tone; leaving the stick at full throttle for longer enters the RC-Setup instead (all small-ESC manuals in this file).

HV V4 (120HV K, 160HV K; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): the model manual names the ProgCard as the main tool and refers stick setup to the YGE RC-setup manual; that this menu applies to these models is inferred from the reference, not stated per model.

HV V4 (120HV K, 160HV K; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): Governor modes are named in the text ('one of the two Gov modes') but no mode menu is listed; the defaults after activating one are timing 18 deg, brake off, active freewheel on, P-gain 0.9, I-gain 0.05, startup speed heli slow, PWM 8 kHz, startup power auto 1-32%.

HV V4 (120HV K, 160HV K; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): Error clearing: connect battery with stick at full power, disconnect after the interval beep while keeping full power; releasing the stick first enters RC-Setup.

FAI (pylon racing / hotliner; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): the model manual names the ProgCard as the main tool and refers stick setup to the YGE RC-setup manual; that this menu applies to these models is inferred from the reference, not stated per model.

FAI (pylon racing / hotliner; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): 150HV FAI partial-load rating: English manual says 100 A for about 5 s, German manual says 90 A for 5 s (YGE_150HV-FAI_en.pdf vs YGE_Bedienungsanleitung-150HV-FAI.pdf).

FAI (pylon racing / hotliner; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): Delivery state stated: timing 18 deg, brake middle, undervoltage cutoff LiPo mode 3.1 V per cell. Brake steps: smooth 0.5 s, middle 0.3 s, hard 0.2 s (150HV and 200HV FAI).
FAI (pylon racing / hotliner; ProgCard / RC-Setup only): The 160 FAI V3 manual gives 3 to 6s LiPo and an adjustable switching BEC; the 300 FAI has no BEC.
